content_text: The Screen Actors Guild Awards (in the original English: Screen Actors Guild Awards, also known as the SAG Awards or simply The Actor) are annual awards presented by the Screen Actors Guild‐American Federation of Television and Radio Artists (SAG-AFTRA) to recognize outstanding performances in film and television. The statuette, a nude male figure holding a comedy mask and a tragedy mask, is called "The Actor" (The Actor). Standing sixteen inches (41 cm) tall and weighing more than twelve pounds (5.4 kg), it is cast in solid bronze and made by the American Fine Arts Foundry in Burbank, California.

Since 1995, the SAG Awards have been one of the major awards events in Hollywood. Nominations come from two committees, one for film and one for television, each made up of 2,100 guild members chosen at random from a total of 165,000 members (as of 2012) eligible to vote. Considered among the most prestigious in the industry, they are a reliable "preview" of the Oscars in the acting categories.

information.contentTitle: I Am An Actor | 26th Annual SAG Awards | TNT

content_text: From 1998 to 2006, they were broadcast by TNT, and since 2007 they have been broadcast by TNT and TBS. The latter also airs them in Latin America, with simultaneous translation into Spanish and, in Brazil's case, into Portuguese. In Portugal, they are broadcast every year by AXN. The inaugural SAG Awards were broadcast live on February 25, 1995. The second edition was broadcast live from the Santa Monica Civic Auditorium, while subsequent ceremonies have been held at the Shrine Auditorium in Los Angeles. On December 4, 2017, it was announced that the ceremony would have its first host in its 24-year history: actress Kristen Bell.
